exact_bilingual_spans.text: وقيل : إن قريشا كانوا يقولون لمن مات ذكور ولده : قد بتر فلان . فلما مات لرسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ابنه القاسم : بمكة ، وإبراهيم بالمدينة ، قالوا : بتر محمد ، [ ص: 198 ] فليس له من يقوم بأمره من بعده ; فنزلت هذه الآية ; قال السدي وابن زيد .

And it is said: The Quraysh used to say of the one whose male children died: "So-and-so has been cut off." When the son of the Messenger of Allah—may Allah's prayers and peace be upon him—al-Qasim died in Mecca, and Ibrahim in Medina, they said: "Muhammad has been cut off, [for] he has no one to manage his affairs after him"; so this verse was revealed, as al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said.

source_witnesses.locator: Surah 108:3, displayed printed page 198; paragraph beginning وقيل إن قريشا كانوا يقولون
supports: shared closing attribution to al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd

source_witnesses.locator: Surah 108:3, al-Qurtubi paragraph ending قال السدي وابن زيد
supports: same combined account and attribution boundary

source_witnesses.locator: Surah 108:3, Ibn Zayd report: حدثني يونس قال أخبرنا ابن وهب قال قال ابن زيد
supports: Ibn Zayd is separately transmitted as explaining that Muhammad was called without posterity
Ibn Abi Hatim attribution from al-Suddi that Quraysh used the expression when a man's sons died
disagrees_or_differs: the named speaker is al-As ibn Wa'il rather than an undifferentiated Quraysh collective
al-Suddi report says only the Prophet's child, without naming both al-Qasim and Ibrahim
al-Qasim is supplied in a separate al-Bayhaqi report from Muhammad ibn Ali
Ibrahim appears in a separate report from Abu Ayyub and another from Ibn Jurayj
no joint Ibn Zayd attribution is recorded

source_witnesses.source: Ibn Adil, al-Lubab fi Ulum al-Kitab
source_witnesses.locator: Surah 108:3, paragraph beginning وقال السدي وابن زيد; note 9
supports: the combined Qurtubi-form account is repeated with al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd attribution
source_witnesses.source_note: Note 9 points to al-Durr al-Manthur and Ibn Abi Hatim from al-Suddi, whose inventoried wording is narrower than the combined account.

fidelity_findings.reason_not_closed: The located source-specific witnesses separately support shorter al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd motifs but do not independently attest Qurtubi's full combined al-Qasim/Ibrahim, Mecca/Medina, Quraysh, dual-attribution account as one report.

explicit_non_assimilation: Do not import al-As ibn Wa'il from the al-Suddi inventory witness into Qurtubi's undifferentiated Quraysh wording.
Do not import the al-Qasim name from al-Bayhaqi/Muhammad ibn Ali into the narrower al-Suddi witness.
Do not import Ibrahim from the Abu Ayyub or Ibn Jurayj reports into either al-Suddi or Ibn Zayd as though one chain carried the combined wording.
Do not merge this span with the preceding Abu Jahl or Uqbah reports or the following Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf report.
